The system takes a photo of a plate and returns a list of the dishes it finds, along with an estimate of calories for each one. We chose YOLOv8 because it detects several objects in one pass and runs on a normal laptop without a graphics card. The training data came from 700 photos that the team took in the college canteen over three weeks. Each photo was labelled by hand using bounding boxes, and the labels were checked by a second team member to reduce mistakes. We split the data into 560 images for training, 70 for validation and 70 for testing. After 50 epochs the model reached a mean average precision of 0.71 on the test set. Calories are estimated by matching each detected dish to an average portion size taken from a published nutrition table. This step is simple, but it means the estimate can be wrong when a portion is much larger or smaller than usual. In future work we plan to use the size of the plate as a reference so that the portion size can be measured from the image itself rather than assumed.
